paper.title: Stochastic Linear Bandits Robust to Adversarial Attacks

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear bandit with adversarially corrupted rewards (known C)
unmapped: adversary observes the chosen action and the noise realization and knows theta before corrupting
settings.definition_quote: Y_t = \langle \theta, A_t \rangle + \epsilon_t + c_t(A_t) ... The total attack budget of the adversary is given by \sum_{t=1}^T |c_t(A_t)| \leq C.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear bandit with adversarially corrupted rewards (unknown C)
unmapped: adversary observes the chosen action and the noise realization and knows theta before corrupting
settings.definition_quote: We will consider both the cases that C is known and unknown to the learner.

settings.name_in_paper: Corrupted linear bandit, known C (lower bound)
settings.definition_quote: For any dimension d, there exists an instance with k = d such that any algorithm (even with knowledge of C) must incur \Omega(Cd) regret

settings.name_in_paper: Corrupted linear bandit, unknown C (lower bound)
settings.definition_quote: For d=2 and k=2, for any algorithm that guarantees R_T \le \bar{R}^{(0)}_T ...

settings.name_in_paper: Linear contextual bandit with smoothed (diverse) contexts and adversarial corruptions
unmapped: contexts are adversarial means plus independent random perturbations (smoothed analysis)
settings.definition_quote: An arbitrary tuple \mu_{1,t}, \dots ,\mu_{K,t} of mean context vectors is given (possibly selected by an adaptive adversary ...), such that \|\mu_{i,t}\|_2\leq 1 ... a_{i,t} = \mu_{i,t} + \xi_{i,t}

source.label: thm:regret_bound
source.quote: For any attack budget $C \ge 0$, with probability at least $1 - \delta$, the Robust Phased Elimination algorithm with known $C$ and truncation parameter $\nu = \tfrac{1}{4d(\log \log d + 18)}$ satisfies R_T = \tilde{O}(\sqrt{dT\log(k/\delta)} + Cd^{3/2}\log T), where the notation $\tilde{O}(\cdot)$ hides $\log\log(dT)$ factors.

results.notes: O_tilde hides loglog(dT) factors only. Regret is realized sum of gaps, bounded w.p. 1-delta.

bound.regime: C <= sqrt(T)/(4d(log log d + 18) log T)

source.label: thm:regret_bound2
source.quote: For any $C \le \frac{\sqrt T}{4d(\log \log d + 18) \log T}$, with probability at least $1 - \delta$, the Robust Phased Elimination algorithm with unknown $C$ and truncation parameter $\nu = \tfrac{1}{4d(\log \log d + 18)}$ satisfies R_T = \tilde{O}(\sqrt{dT\log(k/\delta)} + Cd^{3/2}\log T + C^2).

results.notes: Text after the theorem informally extends to arbitrary C with C^2 d^2 (log T)^2 term; not recorded separately.

conditions: k = d, arms are standard basis vectors

source.label: thm:lower_d
source.quote: For any dimension $d$, there exists an instance with $k = d$ such that any algorithm (even with knowledge of $C$) must incur $\Omega(Cd)$ regret with probability at least $\frac{1}{2}$.

results.notes: Constant probability 1/2, recorded as realized_regret. Proof uses noiseless instances.

symbols.R0_T: uncorrupted regret bound guaranteed by the algorithm w.p. 1-delta when C=0, with R0_T <= T/16

conditions: algorithm guarantees R_T <= R0_T w.p. >= 1-delta when C = 0

source.label: thm:lower_C
source.quote: For $d=2$ and $k=2$, for any algorithm that guarantees $R_T \le \bar{R}^{(0)}_T$ with probability at least $1 - \delta$ for a given uncorrupted regret bound $\bar{R}^{(0)}_T \le \frac{T}{16}$ when $C = 0$, there exists an instance in which $R_T = \Omega(T)$ with probability at least $1-\delta$ when $C = 2 \bar{R}^{(0)}_T$.

results.notes: Algorithm class: algorithms with uncorrupted high-prob regret guarantee R0_T and no knowledge of C.

symbols.lambda_0: diversity parameter of the context perturbations

results.notes: Greedy does not use T or C; but the perturbation condition references T. Horizon marked anytime with that caveat.

symbols.eta_pert: standard deviation of Gaussian context perturbations N(0, eta^2 I)

conditions: Gaussian context perturbations N(0, eta^2 I), independent

source.label: corr:greedy
source.quote: Assume the context perturbations $\xi_{i,t}$ are drawn independently from $\mathcal{N}(0,\eta^2 I)$ for all $i,t$, the reward noise is $1$-sub-Gaussian, and the attack budget of the adversary is $C \geq 0$. Then for a fixed number of arms $k$ and $\eta \leq O((\sqrt{d \log(Tkd/\delta)})^{-1})$, with probability at least $1 - \delta$, the greedy algorithm has regret bounded by ...

results.notes: Paper's eta is the perturbation std, renamed eta_pert to avoid clash with learning-rate symbol.
